Subject: Model fit intake + prompt corpus request — HelixMed

Hi Samantha / Carlos —

Thanks again for the demo today — really appreciate the clear walkthrough of the clinician workflow and where you hit errors. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can put together a targeted eval: 

Key takeaways
- Primary use: summarization + assisted charting for outpatient notes (both structured data + free-text).
- Edge cases you called out: heavily abbreviated notes, mixed languages (EN/ES), legacy ICD-like codes, and snippets with PHI identifiers (MRN).
- Success metrics for the pilot: intent/label accuracy on extraction tasks, hallucination rate < 3% measured on curated QA set, and avg generation latency < 350ms tail for 512-token responses.

Model recommendations (initial):
1) Llama2-13B q4_0 (fp16/quantized) — best balance for contextual accuracy and throughput for your 512-token targets.
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (float32) — faster on shorter responses; lower cost in Dedicated mode but may need guardrails for hallucinations.
3) Fallback: a verified 70B-variant for critical extraction routes where recall is essential (can be routed only for flagged requests).

What we need from you to run the eval:
- Prompt corpus: 150–300 user examples covering normal flows + the edge cases above. Use the attached template (helixmed-prompt-sample-template.csv) — 3 columns: id, user_query, expected_behavior/notes.
- Redaction guidance: mark any prompt rows that contain PHI. If full-text examples contain PHI, please either:
  * provide a redacted version (replace MRNs/user ids with <MRN_####>), or
  * provide hashed IDs (consistent but non-reversible) so we preserve referential integrity across examples.
- A short prioritized list of 10 canonical golden cases we must get right (we’ll use these as canary tests).

Timeline proposal
- Please return populated template by EOD Friday 2027-06-04.
- We’ll run an initial eval (model runs + metrics) and share results in a 48–72 hour turnaround.
- Follow-up call: 30 min sync to review results and suggested routing/quantization — propose Mon 2027-06-07 or Tue 2027-06-08.

Notes on security/compliance (high level)
- We can run in Dedicated or Private for PHI-sensitive data. For the pilot, we recommend Dedicated with customer-managed KMS if you plan to ingest live PHI. Irene can provide SOC2 evidence and a short checklist (cc’d).

Attachments: helixmed-prompt-sample-template.csv (CSV template)

Next steps
1) Fill the template and flag any rows that contain PHI.
2) Share one short sample file (10–15 rows) if you want us to do a quick smoke-run before the full deliverable.
3) Confirm which day/time for the follow-up review call.

If helpful I can also include a short cost estimate for 100k tokens/mo across the two model options — want that in this thread?

Thanks — looking forward to the prompt set.

Best,
Tessa Morgan

2) Languages: we have about ~8% Spanish in the sample set. We will flag language per-row in the template.

Thanks Samantha — this is perfect. A few quick confirmations and a redaction checklist we typically ask for when collecting prompt corpora: 

Redaction checklist (short)
- Remove or replace direct patient identifiers: full names, MRNs, SSNs. Replace with tokens like <MRN_1234> or use consistent hashed IDs.
- Remove free-text addresses and phone numbers; keep length/format metadata if useful (e.g., "address_length": 32).
- For any PHI you must keep for context (rare), provide an isolated redacted and a hashed version — call out which rows must be treated carefully.
- For language flags: add a column lang (en/es).

Prompt set guidance
- Aim for 150–300 rows; include 10–15 golden cases we will use as canaries.
- For each prompt include: id, user_query, expected_behavior (brief), lang, ph_flag (yes/no).
- If examples include structured fields (ICD codes), keep them in a separate column and label as structured_field.

Evaluation priorities
- Primary: extraction precision/recall for structured fields, hallucination rate on free-text summaries, and slot-filling accuracy.
- Secondary: latency tail (p95), token cost per conversation.

We’ll:
- Run an initial smoke-run on the 15-row file you attached and share results within 24 hours.
- Produce an eval report with model recommendations, a small quality regression checklist (prompt-based tests), and a suggested routing policy for canary -> fallback.

Action items (summary)
1) Samantha/Carlos: upload completed CSV (150–300 rows) by EOD 2027-06-04, or confirm if you want us to proceed with the 15-row sample for a quick smoke-run now.
2) Ben/Irene: we’ll collect the SOC2 artifact list and reply to Samantha on dedicated/private tradeoffs.
3) Tessa: I will send cost estimates (hosted vs dedicated) and the initial smoke-run results.

Attachments: helixmed_redaction_checklist.pdf, helixmed-prompt-sample-template.csv

Looking forward — if you want to push the follow-up to Mon 6/7 10am PT I’ve penciled that in.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
